key_insight: This paper proposes a Turing-test-style, human-centered evaluation framework to determine whether video foundation models can function as reliable embodied world models by measuring perceptual fidelity and robustness under realistic interaction scenarios.
problem_solved: Fills the gap in standardized evaluation for assessing whether generative video models preserve perceptual realism for human observers and remain robust across diverse embodied settings before being used in downstream 3D prediction or interactive generation tasks.
method: Design a Turing-test-style human study where observers distinguish model-generated vs. real/ground-truth video continuations to quantify perceptual fidelity.
Assemble a benchmark of embodied scenarios and stress tests (e.g., occlusions, dynamic interactions, distribution shifts) to probe generative generalization and robustness.
Combine human-preference results with automated metrics and robustness curves to produce a comprehensive scorecard for model suitability as an embodied world model.
impact: Provides AI/ML practitioners a clear, human-centered evaluation protocol to decide if a video foundation model is fit for embodied tasks, revealing practical gaps (perceptual failures and brittleness) and guiding model selection and future improvements.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram showing: input scene → video foundation model prediction → human Turing-test (real vs. generated) → aggregated fidelity score
Side-by-side example frames/videos: real vs. model-generated continuations to illustrate perceptual differences
Bar/line charts of human preference rates and automated metric correlations across scenarios and stress conditions
Heatmap or radar chart summarizing robustness across axes (occlusion, interaction complexity, dynamics, domain shift)
paper_title: Wow, wo, val! A Comprehensive Embodied World Model Evaluation Turing Test
paper_authors: Chun-Kai Fan, Xiaowei Chi, Xiaozhu Ju, Hao Li, Yong Bao
